As the study progressed, Alignment B was dropped on the basis that it was no longer a feasible alternate due to the development that had occured along the route. Alignment A was the only one presented at the public hearing.
With Alignment A the Thorn Creek bridge structure is to be replaced because of deterioration, inadequate cross section and hydraulic requirements. In order to provide a new structure the old structure including the existing wing walls must be removed.
Minor local changes in the vertical and horizontal geometrics of Alignment A at Thorn Creek would not eliminate the use of the Forest Preserve District for a temporary construction easement. The wing walls would still require removal with the removal of the old structure. In the same local change context the reconstruction of the Forest Preserve District parking lot entrance would still be necessary inorder to meet a safe gradient and opening width with Lincoln Highway for the safety of the parking lot user.
Therefore, the recommended alternative is "To Improve this Highway Facility" in accordance with Alignment "A". This alignment is considered the most feasible and prudent alternate and even if local minor alignment adjustments were initiated in the area of Thorn Creek the use of Forest Preserve District land by a temporary construction easement cannot be feasibly and prudently avoided.
